evals.name: cloudflare-worker-ai-proxy
evals.prompt: im about to deploy this cloudflare worker (it just forwards chat requests to openai). can you make sure its actually safe before i ship it? i really dont want some random person finding it and running up my openai bill
evals.expected_output: Key moved out of [vars] to a secret binding; auth gate added; rate limiting added; CORS locked to a specific origin instead of *; client input bounded/whitelisted instead of spread directly. Chat report explains fixes, hands off provider billing caps + key rotation.

assertions.text: OPENAI_API_KEY is removed from [vars] in wrangler.toml (not left as a plaintext var)
Code no longer hardcodes the key and reads it from env/secret binding only
Some authentication/authorization gate is added before the upstream OpenAI call
Rate limiting is introduced (CF rate limit rule, KV/DO counter, or equivalent)
Access-Control-Allow-Origin is no longer '*'; restricted to specific origin(s)
Client request body is validated/whitelisted rather than spread (...body) straight to OpenAI
Report tells the user to rotate the exposed key and set provider-side billing/usage caps

evals.name: chrome-extension-summarizer
evals.prompt: final check on my chrome extension before i put it on the web store. it summarizes pages using openai. is it secure?
evals.expected_output: Hardcoded OpenAI key flagged as unfixable in-client and routed to a backend (or clearly handed off); host permissions narrowed from <all_urls>; unused permissions dropped; innerHTML replaced with safe rendering/sanitization; onMessage sender validation added. Report explains why a key in an extension is unsafe and says to rotate it.

assertions.text: The hardcoded OpenAI key is identified as exposed and addressed (removed/relocated to a backend), not merely obfuscated
host_permissions / content_script matches no longer use <all_urls> (narrowed or justified)
Unused permissions (e.g. cookies, webRequest) are removed from the manifest
content.js no longer assigns untrusted content via innerHTML (uses textContent or sanitization)
chrome.runtime.onMessage validates the sender or message shape before acting
Report explains that any key shipped in an extension is public and must be rotated

evals.name: nextjs-registration-app
evals.prompt: getting ready to launch my next.js app, it has user registration. can you lock down the security? worried about people stealing user data or my api key getting leaked
evals.expected_output: NEXT_PUBLIC_ secret leak fixed (key moved server-side, client call proxied); .env removed from tracking + .gitignore'd + rotation hand-off; SQL injection fixed with parameterized query; md5 password hashing replaced with bcrypt/argon2; session cookie gets HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite and stops being trivially forgeable; security headers added; dangerouslySetInnerHTML sanitized. Report covers it all.

assertions.text: NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENAI_API_KEY leak is fixed: key moved server-side, client no longer calls OpenAI directly with it
.env is added to .gitignore and the user is told to rotate the exposed DATABASE_URL/keys
The INSERT in register.js uses a parameterized query instead of string interpolation
Password hashing no longer uses md5; replaced with bcrypt/argon2/scrypt
Session cookie gets HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite attributes (and is no longer a trivially-forgeable base64 of the email)
Security headers are configured (CSP / HSTS / X-Content-Type-Options / X-Frame-Options) in next.config.js or middleware
dangerouslySetInnerHTML with model output is sanitized or removed
